app_role.purpose: Closed initial role vocabulary: admin and researcher. These are application roles, not PostgreSQL login roles.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.code: Application role code: admin or researcher. This is not a PostgreSQL login role; the same person may have both.
columns.label: Display label for the application role; authorization uses code, not this label.

service_rules: Only the seeded admin/researcher codes are allowed. Adding a new application role requires a reviewed migration. Labels do not define permissions.

app_user.purpose: Stable local identity; disabling a user preserves historical authorship.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.display_name: Current displayed name of the person; not unique and not an authentication identifier. Exports capture the displayed name at export time.
columns.active: Whether the local account may use the application. The backend checks this on every request; deactivation preserves authorship.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.

service_rules: Enforce active-account checks on every request; preserve at least one active administrator during role/account changes.

app_user_role.purpose: Many-to-many assignment. One person may hold both roles.

columns.user_id: User receiving the application role; first component of the composite primary key.
columns.role_id: Assigned application role; second component of the composite primary key.

service_rules: Authorize every grant/revocation as an administrative action and record it in audit_event in the same transaction. A user may have no roles, one role or both roles.

audit_event.purpose: Append-only action metadata. Object ID is a polymorphic trace; no scientific answers or secrets belong here.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.actor_user_id: Existing local user who performed or initiated the recorded action. SQL does not check that the account is currently active.
columns.action: Controlled event code. Accepted values are listed below; the backend chooses the code, not the client.
columns.object_type: Controlled type of the affected object. Its compatibility with action is a backend rule, not a cross-field SQL CHECK.
columns.object_id: Required UUID identifying the affected object for audit trace. Polymorphic and deliberately not an FK.
columns.details: Metadata-only JSON object. SQL checks object shape but cannot prevent scientific answers, credentials or secrets; the backend must exclude them.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.

service_rules: Record allowed administrative/share/archive/export actions in the same transaction as the mutation. Choose compatible action/object_type values and supply an existing actor.
Restrict details to necessary metadata; do not store scientific answer payloads, passwords, access tokens or other secrets.

auth_identity.purpose: Verified external identity attached to a local user; issuer + subject identifies one account.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.user_id: Local account associated with this verified external identity. This association cannot be reassigned by an UPDATE.
columns.issuer: Identity-provider issuer identifier. It is paired with subject for uniqueness; no particular OIDC provider is configured by this schema.
columns.subject: Stable subject identifier issued by that provider. Never use display name or email alone to match a local account.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.

service_rules: Attach only identities verified by the configured provider. Provider configuration and authentication are outside this schema; do not link accounts by email alone.

equipment.purpose: Machine catalog. Deactivate instead of deleting; its code and identity are stable.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.code: Stable catalog code. The key definition below specifies its uniqueness scope; updates to this code are forbidden by a trigger.
columns.name: Current machine name. The finalized equipment snapshot preserves its historical displayed name.
columns.description: Optional descriptive text. SQL imposes no length limit on this column.
columns.active: Whether this catalog entry is available for new selections. Deactivation retains the row and existing historical references; eligibility is checked by the backend.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.

service_rules: Require an active machine for a new response; existing saved drafts may continue with a deactivation warning. Serialize metadata changes with snapshot capture.

experiment.purpose: An ordered composition owned by its creator. Empty or incomplete compositions can be saved.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.created_by_user_id: Original researcher who created and owns the experiment; ownership is immutable.
columns.title: Current experiment title. Each export captures the title that existed when that export was requested.
columns.description: Optional descriptive text. SQL imposes no length limit on this column.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.
columns.archived_at: Archive timestamp; NULL means unarchived. The backend controls archive/restore and blocks ordinary edits while archived.

service_rules: The owner controls sharing/archive/restore. Sharing an experiment does not grant access to its source submissions.
Allow empty/incomplete experiments; completeness for export is derived from their steps. Archive freezes ordinary metadata, composition, ordering and pins, not linked submissions.

experiment_export.purpose: One immutable capture and PDF attempt, with per-creator request idempotency.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.experiment_id: Experiment whose composition was captured; retained even if its current steps later change.
columns.created_by_user_id: Researcher who requested this export; part of the request-idempotency uniqueness key.
columns.request_id: UUID for an idempotent export request, unique per requester. The backend also compares request content before treating a repeated key as a replay.
columns.source_lock_version: Positive experiment lock_version captured for this request. Historical version evidence, not an FK or an automatic comparison with the current experiment.
columns.report_format_version: Identifier of the renderer/report format used for this captured report. Frozen with the export; no separate format catalog is assumed.
columns.status: Rendering attempt state: pending, ready or failed. SQL validates output metadata for each state and freezes terminal attempts.
columns.manifest: Immutable complete JSON capture of the report context, order and displayed names. SQL checks only that it is an object; the backend ensures agreement with export items.
columns.pdf_storage_key: Opaque private storage key. NULL while pending/failed; required and nonblank when ready. It is not a public URL or an authorization credential.
columns.pdf_sha256: SHA-256 file digest encoded as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. NULL while pending/failed; required when ready. The backend verifies it against file bytes.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.completed_at: NULL while pending; required completion/failure timestamp for ready/failed. SQL does not enforce chronological ordering against created_at.

service_rules: Capture a nonempty complete experiment with all sources readable, its immutable manifest and all ordered items in one transaction.
Validate request-id replay content, freeze the item set immediately after capture, render only captured content and verify the file hash before ready.
Re-check current rights to the experiment and every historical source on each download, even when current steps were removed.

experiment_export_item.purpose: Ordered reference to an exact revision. Source step ID is historical trace, not a foreign key.

columns.export_id: Parent saved export capture; part of the composite primary key.
columns.position: Positive frozen display order inside this export. Together with export_id identifies one item.
columns.source_step_id: Required UUID tracing the original current step. Deliberately not an FK so deleting the current step preserves this export.
columns.submission_id: Source submission identifier, paired with revision_no to reference one exact immutable revision.
columns.revision_no: Revision of that same submission captured by this export. Not globally unique and not automatically advanced after correction.

service_rules: Create all items with the manifest in the capture transaction. No later additions are allowed by service policy; SQL blocks UPDATE/DELETE but does not block INSERT after capture or completion.
Require contiguous positions and exact agreement with the captured manifest and chosen revisions. The trace UUID does not require a current step to exist.

experiment_grant.purpose: Explicit read/edit grant for an experiment; it grants no implicit access to underlying submissions.

columns.experiment_id: Experiment shared by this current grant; part of the composite primary key.
columns.user_id: Named recipient of the experiment grant. This grant never implicitly shares the experiment’s source submissions.
columns.access_level: Explicit grant level: read or edit. Edit includes read but does not confer sharing, archive or ownership rights.
columns.granted_by_user_id: User who most recently issued or changed the grant. The backend must verify that this actor owns the target object.
columns.granted_at: Timestamp of the current grant issuance; the backend refreshes it when regranting or changing the grant.
columns.revoked_at: NULL means the grant is unrevoked; otherwise this is its revocation time. An unrevoked row alone does not establish authorization.

service_rules: Only the experiment owner may issue, change or revoke this grant. Independently authorize every referenced submission for read/edit/export.
Reuse the same target/recipient row for regrant; refresh grant metadata, clear revoked_at when authorized and append audit events.

experiment_step.purpose: Planned template version, optionally attached to a submission and a selected finalized revision.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.experiment_id: Experiment containing this current step. The step cannot be moved to another experiment by UPDATE.
columns.template_version_id: Required planned template version even before a submission exists. An attached submission must use this same version.
columns.submission_id: Optional attached execution. A non-NULL submission can appear in at most one current step across all experiments.
columns.pinned_revision_no: Optional selected revision number belonging to the attached submission. A non-NULL value requires submission_id; later corrections do not automatically change this pin.
columns.position: Positive order within the experiment. Uniqueness is deferrable to allow reordering; the backend checks final contiguous positions and the 100-step limit.

service_rules: Permit changing the planned version only while no submission is attached. SQL fixes id/experiment_id, not this higher-level transition rule.
Attaching an existing source requires edit on experiment and source, a nonarchived source, matching template version and no other current assignment.

Attach a finalized source with its current revision pinned. First finalization of an attached draft pins revision 1 only if the experiment is active. SQL allows a NULL pin on an attached finalized source.
Later corrections require an explicit pin update with experiment edit and source read. Deleting/detaching a step leaves its submission and all old export items intact.

form_template.purpose: Reusable template identity attached permanently to one machine. Current name follows the latest version title.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.equipment_id: The single machine to which this reusable template belongs. The association is fixed after creation.
columns.created_by_user_id: User who originally created the template. Template-management authorization requires the admin role in the backend.
columns.name: Current template catalog name, synchronized by the backend with the newest definition title. Historical rendering uses the versioned title.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.archived_at: Template archive timestamp. NULL means available, subject to the machine being active. Existing submissions retain their original version.

service_rules: Create the template and its first version in one transaction. SQL permits zero child versions; the service must enforce the initial version.
Create/save versions only for authorized admins. Synchronize name with the newest definition title and check the expected lock_version.

reference_resource.purpose: Administered reference values, initially materials. Stable kind/code; labels are snapshotted on finalization.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.kind: Open text resource category, initially material. This is not a closed SQL enum. The category is fixed after creation.
columns.code: Stable resource code, unique only together with kind. A new identity is required when the resource meaning changes.
columns.label: Human-readable current catalog label. Changing it does not rewrite labels already preserved in historical snapshots.
columns.description: Optional descriptive text. SQL imposes no length limit on this column.
columns.active: Whether this catalog entry is available for new selections. Deactivation retains the row and existing historical references; eligibility is checked by the backend.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.

service_rules: Authorize catalog administration and serialize changes with snapshot capture. New selections must be active and allowed; retain an inactive saved choice only with proof at the same submission/field/instance/ID.

resource_group.purpose: Reusable group restricting available reference values.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.code: Stable catalog code. The key definition below specifies its uniqueness scope; updates to this code are forbidden by a trigger.
columns.label: Human-readable current catalog label. Changing it does not rewrite labels already preserved in historical snapshots.
columns.active: Whether this group is eligible for new reference selections. Saved inactive choices require backend proof of prior use in the same field/instance.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.

service_rules: Validate group eligibility when saving definitions or new choices; check member and resource eligibility as well. Deactivation does not delete memberships.

resource_group_member.purpose: Membership and display order. A removed member becomes inactive; the link is retained.

columns.group_id: Group containing the resource; first component of the retained membership primary key.
columns.resource_id: Resource included in the group; second component of the retained membership primary key.
columns.position: Positive display position, unique within the group only for active memberships. Inactive rows may reuse a position.
columns.active: Whether this membership currently permits new selections. Remove a membership by setting false, rather than deleting its row.

service_rules: Require a valid active group, member and resource for new selections. A saved inactive membership may be retained only with occurrence-level proof.
Reorder active members transactionally using temporary positive positions or temporary deactivation. This partial unique index is not deferrable.

submission.purpose: One research execution; mutable draft or synchronized current finalized revision. Creator is the owner.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.template_version_id: Exact template version used for this execution; fixed for drafts, finalization and every later correction.
columns.created_by_user_id: Original researcher who created this execution and owns it. Ownership is immutable.
columns.status: draft or submitted. Finalization requires a current revision, project/sample context, snapshots and first-submission timestamp.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.current_revision_no: NULL for a draft; positive current finalized revision number for submitted. Together with this row id, references a revision of this same submission.
columns.project_reference: System project context: optional in draft, required when submitted; 1–200 characters when present, without leading/trailing whitespace. Not a catalog FK or unique key.
columns.sample_reference: System sample context: optional in draft, required when submitted; 1–200 characters when present, without leading/trailing whitespace. Does not define ownership or inventory membership.
columns.answers: Current JSON answer object. Drafts retain saved hidden fields/inactive repeat instances; submitted content is the active projection synchronized with the current revision by the backend.
columns.equipment_snapshot: Historical equipment context JSON object. SQL permits NULL or an object in draft, but requires an object when submitted. Snapshot completeness is a backend rule.
columns.reference_snapshot: Historical resource/unit context JSON object. Optional in draft, required when submitted; an empty object is valid when no references are used.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.
columns.submitted_at: NULL for a draft; time of first finalization for a submitted execution. A trigger preserves it through all later corrections.
columns.archived_at: Archive timestamp; NULL means unarchived. The backend controls archive/restore and blocks ordinary edits while archived.

service_rules: Merge explicit draft changes without erasing omitted hidden values. Finalization computes the active projection and validates all system context.

Insert each new revision and synchronize current answers, snapshots and project/sample context atomically. Require exactly the next revision number; SQL does not prove current-copy equality or +1 progression.
A draft has zero finalized revisions by service policy; SQL does not prohibit a raw INSERT into submission_revision while its parent is still draft.
Check active researcher, ownership/edit access, archive state and expected lock_version with the mutation. Archives do not revoke otherwise authorized history reads.

submission_grant.purpose: Explicit read/edit grant to one named user; revocation retains the current grant row.

columns.submission_id: Submission shared by this current grant; part of the composite primary key.
columns.user_id: Named recipient of the submission grant. Read permits finalized history; edit also permits drafts and corrections, subject to current authorization.
columns.access_level: Explicit grant level: read or edit. Edit includes read but does not confer sharing, archive or ownership rights.
columns.granted_by_user_id: User who most recently issued or changed the grant. The backend must verify that this actor owns the target object.
columns.granted_at: Timestamp of the current grant issuance; the backend refreshes it when regranting or changing the grant.
columns.revoked_at: NULL means the grant is unrevoked; otherwise this is its revocation time. An unrevoked row alone does not establish authorization.

service_rules: Only the submission owner may issue, change or revoke this grant. Require an active researcher recipient for research access.
Reuse the same target/recipient row for regrant; refresh grant metadata, clear revoked_at when authorized and append audit events. The row is not the complete grant history.

submission_revision.purpose: Immutable finalized answers and context. Revision numbers are local to a submission.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.submission_id: Execution whose finalized state is captured. The pair with revision_no is the natural revision key.
columns.revision_no: Positive revision number within that submission. Revision 1 is the first finalization; later consecutive numbers are allocated by the backend.
columns.created_by_user_id: Researcher who finalized this revision, including an authorized editor; may differ from the execution owner.
columns.correction_reason: Optional explanation of a correction, at most 1,000 characters. SQL does not require it or restrict it to revisions after the first.
columns.project_reference: Immutable project context for this revision; required, 1–200 characters, no leading/trailing whitespace.
columns.sample_reference: Immutable sample context for this revision; required, 1–200 characters, no leading/trailing whitespace.
columns.answers: Complete immutable active answer projection at this finalization. Old revisions are not modified by later corrections.
columns.equipment_snapshot: Immutable equipment identity/code/name context; required JSON object. Corrections retain the base equipment context by backend policy.
columns.reference_snapshot: Immutable resource/unit contexts used by active answers. Required JSON object; may be empty when no resource/unit is used.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.

service_rules: Create revision 1 at first finalization, then append one full revision per accepted correction. Validate full active content and authoritative snapshots before insertion.
Retain the equipment context on correction; retain known per-ID reference contexts from the expected current base and capture newly used IDs. Never replace old snapshots with live catalog labels.

template_version.purpose: Immutable definition including title, instructions, fields, options and rules. Version numbers are local to a template.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.template_id: Reusable template whose definition is frozen by this row.
columns.version_no: Positive version number within one template; not globally unique. The backend allocates consecutive numbers under the template lock.
columns.created_by_user_id: Author of this version. May differ from the original template creator.
columns.definition: Complete immutable JSON object containing schema format, title, instructions, ordered field nodes, options and rules. SQL checks object shape only.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.

service_rules: Validate all nodes, field IDs, types, options, rule dependencies and reference choices. Allocate version numbers consecutively under the template lock; SQL guarantees positivity and uniqueness, not sequence.

unit.purpose: Unit vocabulary. Code and dimension are stable; no conversion table is assumed.

columns.id: Stable UUID identifying this row. Generated on insertion unless supplied by trusted server code.
columns.code: Stable catalog code. The key definition below specifies its uniqueness scope; updates to this code are forbidden by a trigger.
columns.symbol: Current unit symbol used for display. Historical revisions retain the captured symbol.
columns.label: Human-readable current catalog label. Changing it does not rewrite labels already preserved in historical snapshots.
columns.dimension: Stable open text dimension, such as mass. This is not a SQL enum; the backend validates dimension compatibility and allowed units.
columns.active: Whether this catalog entry is available for new selections. Deactivation retains the row and existing historical references; eligibility is checked by the backend.
columns.lock_version: Positive optimistic-concurrency counter. The backend compares the expected value and increments it on successful mutations; SQL only checks positivity.
columns.created_at: Server-controlled creation timestamp; the SQL default is the start time of the inserting transaction.
columns.updated_at: Timestamp of the latest successful mutation. The backend must set it on updates; there is no automatic update trigger.

service_rules: Validate numeric value separately from unit identity and dimension. No unit conversion or silent rounding is included.
